abstract: Health management is often a collective activity, involving family members and close relations in monitoring, interpreting, and coordinating care. Yet, most digital health technologies remain individual-centric, offering limited support for the distributed responsibilities and negotiated information sharing that characterize collective care. We present JEEVHITAA, a human-centered AI ecosystem designed to address this gap. Drawing on existing literature on collective health practices, we identify key requirements and translate them into a canonical ontology and a versioned data schema that underpin a mobile ecosystem integrating wearable data, role-aware sharing, granular access controls, auditable histories, and AI-assisted health summarization and verification. We first evaluated core system primitives using 1,000 ontology-driven synthetic care circles to test data visibility and information-processing workflows. We then conducted a controlled lab study with 13 subject--care-actor dyads (26 participants), combining task-based interactions, semi-structured interviews, the System Usability Scale, and component-level usability assessments. Findings indicate positive perceptions of usability and highlight the value of granular sharing and transparent information provenance. They also expose tensions between reciprocal transparency and surveillance, and between AI-mediated assistance and potentially intrusive notifications. We discuss implications for designing accountable, context-sensitive technologies that support collective care.

ur.tldr: 面向家庭与亲友协同照护，构建整合可穿戴数据、角色化共享、细粒度权限、可审计历史及AI健康摘要与核验的生态系统。基于合成照护圈和26人实验室研究显示，系统可用性较好，但互惠透明、监控风险及通知侵扰之间仍存在张力。

title: Developing JEEVHITAA: Designing and Evaluating a Human-Centered AI Ecosystem for Collective Care
title_zh: 开发JEEVHITAA：面向集体照护的人本AI生态系统设计与评估
